question: Where can I get the official zoning that classifies land for renewable energy siting in the United States, such as environmental sensitivity maps or renewables acceleration areas, as geometry, with category and the technologies it applies to?

answer.summary: No nationwide official renewable-siting zoning was found. BLM publishes open ArcGIS services for its western public lands: 153 solar energy zone polygons, California DRECP development focus areas (171, with a technology class) and variance lands (7), and the 2024 Final Solar PEIS analysis (9,966,036 polygons flagged Excluded or Other). The 2024 Western Solar Plan makes over 31 million acres available. California's CEC publishes dissolved solar and wind exclusion footprints for planning, not for siting. Texas CREZ geometry was not found. Resource-potential layers are different objects.
main_caveats: BLM layers cover federal lands in western states only. State, local and private-land rules for renewables were barely examined (only California's CEC).
Layers mix object types: preference areas (DFA, SEZ), conditional lands (variance), an exclusion analysis (Solar PEIS), hub points (WGA) and resource potential. They are not one classification.
BLM's FAQ says the 2024 plan eliminates variance lands as a category, yet the DRECP layer still lists 7 variance polygons; the final-plan map layer was not identified.
CEC land-use screens 'should not be used, on their own, to guide siting'; each layer is one dissolved polygon with no category field.
The Solar PEIS analysis layer (9.97 million polygons, edited 2024-08-21) is solar only and its Excluded/Other totals were not reconciled with the official 31 million acres.
answer.confidence_reason: BLM and CEC services were queried live; effects come from BLM and CEC texts; few states examined, final 2024 plan layer not identified, Texas CREZ geometry not found.

attributes.note: Official polygons for BLM solar energy zones, DRECP DFAs, the 2024 Solar PEIS analysis and CEC exclusion footprints; none nationwide; CEC layers are single dissolved polygons.
attributes.gap_note: Only BLM western lands and California's CEC were tested. Next: other states' energy offices and county renewable overlay districts; Texas CREZ geometry (PUCT/ERCOT PDFs returned 403) and the final 2024 plan layer.

attributes.note: DFA/variance classes, SEZ Developable/Non-developable status and PEIS Excluded/Other flags; effects come from the DRECP ROD, the Western Solar Plan FAQ and press release.
attributes.gap_note: Meaning of the PEIS exclusion codes (e01-e21) and of SEZ status values was not read in the PEIS/ROD documents; CEC layers carry no category field.

attributes.note: DRECP Technology values (All Technologies, Geothermal, Solar and Geothermal); Solar PEIS and SEZ are solar only; CEC has separate solar and wind layers.
attributes.gap_note: No wind classification from BLM was found; Argonne's wind exclusion maps (wwmp.anl.gov) returned 403; technologies of AZ REDAs were not checked.
